en: O Aśvins, come, passing by all the other sacrificers, so that I, the seer, may always overcome all the offspring hostile to us. Or else: "tiraḥ" has the sense of "attained" (Ni. 3-20); the meaning is that I may perform all your rites that have come to me. The two are everlasting; they are destroyers of enemies; they ride in a golden chariot; they have good wealth; they make the rivers flow by impelling the rain. Such as you are, come passing by the others.
- हिरण्यवर्तनी (*hiraṇyavartanī*)—who have a chariot made of gold
- सिंधुवाहसा (*siṃdhuvāhasā*)—who impel the flow of the rivers
- अत्यायातं (*atyāyātaṃ*)—leaving all the other sacrificers, favour me alone
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—having rejected (help me to scorn them)
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvins, perfect in the madhuvidyā

O Aśvin deities, destroyers of enemies, who have a golden chariot, excellent wealth, and who impel the flow of the rivers, leave all the other sacrificers and favour me alone. Help me so that I may always reject and drive far away all adversaries. O Aśvins, perfect in the madhuvidyā, listen to my praise.
Passing by (other worshippers), come, Aswins, hither, so that I may ever overcome all (adversaries): Dasras, riding in a golden chariot,
distributors of wealth, propellers of rivers, masters of mystic lore, hear my invocation.

O Aśvins, you two, bearing for us delightful wealth, come to us. O Rudras: sons of Rudra, or else those worthy of praise. O you who have wealth of food, you who ride in a golden chariot, taking pleasure in the sacrifice, serving it, come. The meaning of "mādhvī" and the rest has been given.
- हिरण्यवर्तनी (*hiraṇyavartanī*)—who have a chariot made of gold
- वाजिनीवसू (*vājinīvasū*)—who are endowed with the wealth of food
- आ गच्छतं (*ā gacchataṃ*)—favour us with your presence
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities, perfect in the madhuvidyā

O Aśvin deities, sons of Rudra, who have a chariot made of gold, who partake of the sacrifice and are endowed with the wealth of food, having obtained delightful riches for us, favour us with your presence. O Aśvin deities, perfect in the madhuvidyā, listen to my praise.
Come, Aswins, bring for us precious treasures: Rudras, riding in a golden chariot, propitiated (by sacrifice), affluent with food, masters of mystic lore, hear my invocation.
रुद्रा (*rudrā*)—How the Aśvin deities are sons of Rudra has not been explained by the commentator.

O showerers of riches, O Aśvins, the praise in the form of speech of me, the good praiser, is placed on your chariot; the meaning is that it has been made by us. Moreover, the great seeker, the embodied sacrificer, makes for you the food, the oblation. Therefore hear my invocation.
- वृषण्वसू (*vṛṣaṇvasū*)—O Aśvin deities, who provide riches
- वापुषः (*vāpuṣaḥ*)—who has a human body, the sacrificer
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities, endowed with the madhuvidyā

O Aśvin deities, who provide riches, the praise of me, the excellent praiser, is made and recited addressed to your chariot. And the sacrificer, who seeks you alone, who has special qualities and a human body, offers the oblation. O Aśvin deities, endowed with the madhuvidyā, listen to my invocation in the form of praise.

Showerers of wealth, the praise of your worshipper is addressed to your chariot; (to it), as well as to you, does this distinguished, devoted, embodied (adorer) offer sacrificial food: masters of mystic lore, hear my invocation.

O Aśvins, you whose minds are attentive, who are lords of the chariot, swift-going or else to be approached by all, who hear the invocation, that is, the praise: you go with your horses to the ṛṣi Cyavāna, who is free of duplicity. Just as you came to that ṛṣi, so come on the way to me; come down to me fully. Sāyaṇa says that this is also stated in "प्र च्यवानाज्जु जुरुषो वव्रिं (*pra cyavānājju juruṣo vavriṃ*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-74-5)⟨NOTE:69⟩**GLOSS**
notes: ನೂನಂ glossed ಈ ಯಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ; Sāyaṇa: ನೂನಮದ್ಯ

en: - बोधिन्मनसा (*bodhinmanasā*)—having minds that understand our praise
- अद्वयाविनं (*advayāvinaṃ*)—who, single-minded, was meditating on you alone
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā

O Aśvin deities, having minds that understand our praise, being lords of the chariot, swift-going, hearers of our invocation, you set out with your horses to the sage Cyavana, who, single-minded, was meditating on you alone. O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā, listen to my invocation.
With mind attentive (to praise), riding in cars, swif-tmoving, listening to invocations, you hastened with your steeds to the single-purposed Chyavana : masters of mystic lore, hear my invocation.

The sage Cyavana was old. His body was full of the marks of old age, such as grey hair and a wrinkled body. Because of this, the sons and others of this sage had abandoned him. Then the sage Cyavana praised the Aśvin deities and pleased them, lost his old age through them and obtained youth: this history is told here by this Ṛk. Skandasvāmin has told this history in a different way. This history is seen in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.

Here, in the Śatapatha (Śa. Brā. 4-1-5): अधीतमितिहासमाचक्षते । शर्यातो नाम राजा संक्रीडद्भिः कृतापराधाय कुपिताय जीर्णाय च्यवनाय प्रत्यापत्त्यर्थं सुकन्यां नाम कन्यकां दुहितरं ददौ । तां तत्रासीनां दृष्ट्वा अश्विनौ पुनः पुनरूचतुः । किं किं जीर्णीकृतरूपं कामयसे । आवां संभजेति । सा तौ प्रत्युवाच । यस्मै मां पिता अदात् नाहं तं जीवंतं हास्यामीति । तदृषिज्ञात्वा सुकन्यामुवाच । यदि त्वामेतौ पुनरेवं ब्रूयातां ततस्त्वमेनौ प्रतिब्रूयाः । आसर्वौ वसुसमृद्धौ संतौ पतिं मे निंदथ इति। तौ यदि त्वां प्रतिब्रूयातां केनासर्वौ वसुसमृद्धौ चेति तत एनौ प्रतिब्रूयाः पतिं मे पुनः युवानं कुरुतं । अथ नां वक्ष्यामीति । सा तौ तथोवाच । तामश्विन् प्रत्यूचतुः एतं ह्रदमवतरतु आतो यत् कामयते तेन वयसा युक्त उत्तरिष्यतीति । स ऋषिस्तं ह्रदमवतीयोत्ततार युवाभूत्वेति । तदेतदितिहासेनोच्यते जुजुरुषो नासत्येत्यादिना ॥ (*adhītamitihāsamācakṣate | śaryāto nāma rājā saṃkrīḍadbhiḥ kṛtāparādhāya kupitāya jīrṇāya cyavanāya pratyāpattyarthaṃ sukanyāṃ nāma kanyakāṃ duhitaraṃ dadau | tāṃ tatrāsīnāṃ dṛṣṭvā aśvinau punaḥ punarūcatuḥ | kiṃ kiṃ jīrṇīkṛtarūpaṃ kāmayase | āvāṃ saṃbhajeti | sā tau pratyuvāca | yasmai māṃ pitā adāt nāhaṃ taṃ jīvaṃtaṃ hāsyāmīti | tadṛṣijñātvā sukanyāmuvāca | yadi tvāmetau punarevaṃ brūyātāṃ tatastvamenau pratibrūyāḥ | āsarvau vasusamṛddhau saṃtau patiṃ me niṃdatha iti| tau yadi tvāṃ pratibrūyātāṃ kenāsarvau vasusamṛddhau ceti tata enau pratibrūyāḥ patiṃ me punaḥ yuvānaṃ kurutaṃ | atha nāṃ vakṣyāmīti | sā tau tathovāca | tāmaśvin pratyūcatuḥ etaṃ hradamavataratu āto yat kāmayate tena vayasā yukta uttariṣyatīti | sa ṛṣistaṃ hradamavatīyottatāra yuvābhūtveti | tadetaditihāsenocyate jujuruṣo nāsatyetyādinā ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 4-1-5)

The king named Śaryāti, angered because his sons were playing, gave his daughter named Sukanyā in marriage to the old sage Cyavana. When Sukanyā was living in the hermitage of the sage Cyavana, the Aśvin deities came there and said to her many times: "Abandon this old husband and marry us." To this she said: "My father gave me to this sage. As long as the one who married me is alive, I shall not abandon him." The sage Cyavana heard this and told her: "When they question you again in this way, ask them: 'Though you are endowed with every prosperity, what is the reason that you reproach my husband?' In answer they will ask you: 'How are we rich in wealth?' Then tell them: 'Give my husband youth; afterwards I shall tell you.'" Thus the sage Cyavana taught her what to say to them. Sukanyā spoke to the Aśvin deities as the sage Cyavana had said. Hearing her words, the Aśvin deities said: "If your husband descends into this pool and bathes, your wish will be fulfilled; your husband will become possessed of youth." Having heard the words spoken by the Aśvin deities, he bathed in the pool they had named and came up a young man. This history is told by the Ṛk beginning "jujuruṣo nāsatya". The matter of the Aśvin deities making the old sage Cyavana young is described in many places in the Ṛgveda:
युवं च्यवानं जरसोऽमुमुक्तं नि पेदव ऊहधुराशुमश्वं । (*yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ jaraso 'mumuktaṃ ni pedava ūhadhurāśumaśvaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-71-5)**GLOSS**
प्र च्यवानाज्जु जुरुषो वव्रिमत्कं न मुंचथः । (*pra cyavānājju juruṣo vavrimatkaṃ na muṃcathaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-74-5)**GLOSS**
निष्पौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात्पुनश्च त्वापानं चक्रधुर्युवानं । (*niṣpaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrātpunaśca tvāpānaṃ cakradhuryuvānaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-6)**GLOSS**
युवं च्यवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनर्युनानं चरथाय तक्षथुः । (*yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ sanayaṃ yathā rathaṃ punaryunānaṃ carathāya takṣathuḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-4)**GLOSS**
This matter is mentioned in these Ṛks, and in many other Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-74-5 and 7-68-6.

O Naras, leaders of rites, O Aśvins, let your horses, which are yoked by mere thought, that is, are well trained, of variegated form, swift-going, bring you for the drinking of Soma. Let them bring you together with comforts, that is, with the pleasures to be given to us, or with wealth and the like, which are the means of them.
- मनोयुजः (*manoyujaḥ*)—those that join the chariot by mere resolve
- सुम्मेभिः सह (*summebhiḥ saha*)—with wealth that is to be given to us and gives comfort
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā

O Aśvin deities, leaders, let your horses, which join the chariot by mere resolve, are of wondrous form and are swift-going, bring you for the drinking of Soma, together with wealth that is to be given to us and gives comfort. O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā, listen to my invocation.

Aswins, leaders (of rites), may your horses, harnessed at will, of wondrous beauty, and of rapid course, bring you hither with good gifts to drink (of the proffered beverage): masters of mystic lore, hear my invocation.

O Aśvins, come here, to this sacrifice. O Nāsatyas, do not be without desire: do not become ones whose desire has gone. "Venati" is a word for a verb of desire. O inviolable, worshipful, masters, you two: from a distant place, even one hidden from sight, come to our house of sacrifice, that is, approach it.
- मा वि वेनतं (*mā vi venataṃ*)—do not be unwilling to come to us
- तिरश्चित् (*tiraścit*)—even from a distant place hidden from the eye
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvins, skilled in the madhuvidyā

O Aśvin deities, come to this sacrifice. O Nāsatyas, do not be unwilling to come to us. You who are unharmed and are worshipful lords, come to our house of sacrifice even from a distant place hidden from the eye. O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā, listen to my invocation.
Aswins, come hither : Nasatyas, be not unpropitious : invincible lords, come from hidden (regions) to our sacrificial hall : master of mystic lore, hear my invocation.
O inviolable, that is, unharmable ones, O Śubhaspatis, lords of water, O Aśvins: you at this sacrifice approach me, the praiser, who am eager for help and who extol you; that is, come near.
- गृणंतं (*gṛṇaṃtaṃ*)—the reciter of praise, who extols you
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā

O Aśvin deities, who are free from harm and are lords of water, favour me in this sacrifice, me who am the maker of praise and extol you with praises. O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā, listen to my praise.
Invincible Aswins, lords of water, favour Avasyu, glorifying you at this sacrifice : masters of mystic lore, hear my invocation.

The dawn, that is, the break of day, has come. Agni too is रुशत्पशुः (*ruśatpaśuḥ*): he has shining animals, that is, his oblation is made bright. Or else, "animals" are rays: having shining rays, he has been placed on the altar. This is the Āhavanīya fire, born at the proper season. O showerers of wealth, who give wealth, O Dasras, your immortal chariot, whose nature is not to die, and which is steady, has been yoked; the meaning is that it should be yoked with horses. Here the aorist is used in the sense of a prayer. The meaning of "mādhvī" and the rest has been given.
- ऋत्वियः (*ṛtviyaḥ*)—who appears in accordance with the season
- रुशत्पशुः (*ruśatpaśuḥ*)—who has a shining flame; Agni
- अधायि (*adhāyi*)—has been established on the altar
- दस्रौ (*dasrau*)—who have a form fair to see, O Aśvin deities
- माध्वी (*mādhvī*)—O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā

The goddess Dawn has appeared. Agni, who appears in accordance with the season and has a shining flame, has been established on the altar. O Aśvin deities, givers of wealth, who have a form fair to see, your steady chariot is yoked with horses. O Aśvin deities, skilled in the madhuvidyā, give ear to my invocation.

The dawn has come: the Agni of the season, blazing with the oblation, has been placed (upon the altar): showerers of wealth, subduers of foes, your immortal chariot has been harnessed: masters of mystic lore, hear my invocation.

Agni, who is the face of the dawns, that is, who is awakened at dawn, shines; or else he lights up the face of the dawns, for at the time of dawn the fires are kindled. Moreover, the speeches, that is, the hymns, of the wise praisers, which long for the gods, have risen up. Since this is so, O Aśvins, lords of the chariot, turned toward us, come here today, to this day of the sacrifice. Come to what? To the घर्मं (*gharmaṃ*) that is kindled, the sacrifice, which is full with all its parts; or else to the Soma juice that has swollen, flowing with the vasatīvarī waters; or else, swollen with ghee and the like, to the Pravargya, the ghārma. The use of this sūkta is in the Pravargya.
- आ भाति (*ā bhāti*)—has made to shine
- रथ्या (*rathyā*)—who are lords of the chariot
- पीपिवांसं (*pīpivāṃsaṃ*)—which is full with all its materials
notes: ಕಿಮರ್ಥವಾಗಮ್ಯತೇ ಪೂರ್ವಮೇವಾನೈರ್ದೇವೈಃ ಸ್ವೀಕೃತತ್ವಾತ್ ನೇತ್ಯಾಹ unclear in the machine-read text

en: Agni has appeared and has made the divine faces of the dawn goddesses shine. The wise poets have made and brought to light hymns that praise the gods. O Aśvin deities, lords of the chariot, on this day of the sacrifice come, turned toward us, to this sacrifice, which is full with all its materials and kindled.

Agni lights up the face of the dawns: the devout praisers of the pious have risen up : therefore, Aswins, lords of the chariot, descending, come hither to-day to the splendid sacrifice, perfect (in all its parts).

The Aśvins do not diminish the perfected ghārma; they do not harm it. Rather, near it, now, here in the sacrifice, may they, O Aśvins, who are most inclined to come, be praised. At the break of the day, that is, at the morning time, may you be most inclined to come with protection. Toward अवर्तिं (*avartiṃ*)⟨NOTE:72⟩: "varti" is livelihood, and "avarti" is its absence; come so that food is free of it. And having come, be producers of happiness for the sacrificer who has given the oblation.
notes: ಕಿಂ ತೂಷ್ಣೀಂ । ನ । in the bhāṣya is unclear

en: - संस्कृतं (*saṃskṛtaṃ*)—this ghārma, which has been prepared and made ready
- न प्र मिमीतः (*na pra mimītaḥ*)—do not destroy
- इह अंति (*iha aṃti*)—in this part of the sacrifice
- दिवा अभिपित्वे (*divā abhipitve*)—at the beginning of the day
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who gives the oblation

O Aśvin deities, do not destroy this ghārma (the sacrifice called Pravargya), which has been prepared and made ready. Come to this sacrifice and be worthy of our praise. At the beginning of the day, come with protection that checks poverty and be givers of happiness to the sacrificer who gives the oblation.

Harm not, Aswins, the perfected (rite), but coming now most quickly, be glorified on this occasion : be present at the opening of the day, with protection against destitution, and be prompt to bestow happines upon the donor (of the offering).

The day has equal divisions in two, three, five and fifteen ways; here the fivefold division is taken. "Utāpi ca": also come. When? At the time of saṃgava, the time when the cows gather at the milking place. For in the latter part of the night the cows eat the frosty grass in the forest and return at saṃgava to be milked again; so also in the morning. So also at midday, in the middle of the day, and at the sun's rising and rising, that is, at the time of the sun's greatest growth, which means the afternoon; this also indicates the evening. Not only at the times mentioned, but by day and by night, always, come with most pleasant protection, or on account of the oblation. For what purpose would you come, since the sacrifice had already been accepted before by the other gods? ⟨NOTE:73⟩ He says "no": even now the drinking of the other gods has not been extended, leaving the Aśvins aside; this is what is to be supplied.
notes: ಪಶ್ ಹವಿಷೋ in the bhāṣya is unclear

en: - संगवे (*saṃgave*)—at the time when the cows are milked
- उदिता (*uditā*)—at the evening time, the time of the rising prosperity
- दिवा नक्तं (*divā naktaṃ*)—by day or by night, whichever time it may be
- इदानीं (*idānīṃ*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- पीतिः (*pītiḥ*)—the invitation to the drinking of Soma
- न आ ततान (*na ā tatāna*)—has not been extended to any other deity, leaving the Aśvin deities aside (it has not been appointed)

O Aśvin deities, whether at the time when the cows are milked, at the morning time, at midday, or at the evening time, the time of the sun's rising prosperity, by day or by night, whichever time it may be, come with protection full of happiness. At this time of the sacrifice the invitation to the drinking of Soma has not been extended to any other deity, leaving the Aśvin deities aside.

Whether you come at the (milking time) of the cattle, at the dawn of day, at noon, when the sum is high, or by day or by night, (come) with felicitious protection : the drinking of the Soma has not now extended beyond the Aswins.

O Aśvins, this is your ancient dwelling from of old, a place fit for residence, called the northern altar. Then, with the Saumika altar in view, he says: "These houses, the eastern halls, …" (the sentence continues in the next window).

"These houses, the eastern halls and the rest": this is the house of divine sacrifice, the dwelling. For us, from the sky, from the great mountain, that is, from the cloud, the cause of waters, from the atmosphere: come, that is, arrive. ⟨NOTE:74⟩ Bringing food and strength: strength means the power, and food is the means of power, the essential thing; bearing such a thing, come.
notes: ಘೃತಸ್ಸುರುದಕಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಸನ್ನವೋ unclear in the machine-read text

en: O Aśvin deities, this very region is for you an ancient place fit for residence. These are your houses, this is your place of sacrifice. From the great heavenly world, filled with water and covered with clouds, come for us, bearing food and strength.
This station, Aswins, is your ancient abode; these are your mansions, this your dwelling: come from the vast firmament, (overspread) by clouds (filled) with water, bringing to us food and strength.

May we be united with the new protection of the Aśvins, not made by another, which is the producer of happiness, and with their good guidance, that is, their good coming; or else both are qualifiers of the protection. Bring wealth to us, and bring heroes too, sons and the rest. O immortals, you whose nature is not to die, bring all good fortunes.
- सुप्रणीता (*supraṇītā*)—which is excellent and a guide
- सं गमेम (*saṃ gamema*)—may we be united
- अमृता (*amṛtā*)—O Aśvins, free from the nature of death
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—heroic sons and the rest; favour us with them

May we be united with the new protection of the Aśvin deities, which brings happiness and is an excellent guide. O Aśvins, free from the nature of death, bring about for us all good fortunes. Provide wealth. Favour us with heroic sons and the rest.
May we be united with the Aswins by their special protection, which is the source of happiness and guide to good: bestow upon us, immortals, wealth and posterity. and all good things.

O my priests, worship the two Aśvins who come at dawn, who are first, that is, earlier than the other gods, or the most excellent. For what purpose? The command to sacrifice to them first is stated: let them drink before the greedy one who desires, the non-giver, the demon and the like. If they have not yet come, how can they be worshipped? Therefore he says: the Aśvins

at dawn indeed bear the sacrifice, that is, they share in it. The former seers, the sharers of old, the poets, that is, the ṛṣis who are anūcāna, praise them at dawn alone. He cites ये वा अनूचानास्ते कवयः (*ye vā anūcānāste kavayaḥ*) (Ai. Brā. 2-38)**GLOSS** as the Vedic passage.
- प्रार्यावाणा (*prāryāvāṇā*)—addressing the Aśvin deities who come at dawn
- प्र शंसंति (*pra śaṃsaṃti*)—praise them at dawn alone

Perform the sacrifice addressing the Aśvin deities, who come at dawn, earlier than the other gods. Let them drink the Soma before the greedy, obstructing demon. The Aśvin deities bear the share of the sacrifice at dawn alone. The sages of former times also praise them at dawn alone.

Worship the two who come first (of the gods) at dawn : let them drink before the greedy withholders (of the offering); for the Aswins verily claim the morning sacrifice: the ancient sages praised them (at dawn).

O my men, worship the Aśvins at dawn alone; that is, honour and praise them. Send them oblations. In the evening, the oblation does not go to the gods, it is not; that is, the gods do not accept it. It is unfit to be served. The śruti says पूर्वाणो वै देवानामिति (*pūrvāṇo vai devānāmiti*)**GLOSS**. Moreover, if anyone other than ourselves sacrifices with Soma and satisfies with the oblation, then among us and the others the sacrificer who is earlier and earlier is the most to be honoured, the one whom the gods hold in regard.
- सायं (*sāyaṃ*)—the oblation offered in the evening
- अजुष्टं (*ajuṣṭaṃ*)—the oblation offered at that time is not fit to be enjoyed
- वि चावः (*vi cāvaḥ*)—or offers an oblation (whether among us or among others)
- पूर्वः पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ*)—who offers before all

Addressing the Aśvin deities, offer at dawn alone a praise worthy of worship, and an oblation. An oblation offered in the evening is not pleasing to the gods; an oblation offered at that time is not fit to be enjoyed. Moreover, even if another than ourselves worships, or offers an oblation, whether among us or among others, the sacrificer who offers before all becomes worthy of the love of these gods.
Worship the Aswins at early dawn; offer them oblations: the evening is not for the gods; it is unacceptable to them; and whether it be
any other than ourselves who worships them or propitiates them, the worshipper who is foremost (in his dovotion) is the most approved of.

This verse, "hiraṇyatvak", is the yājyā of the Aśvina offering ⟨NOTE:75⟩; so it is prescribed in the sūtra beginning हिरण्यत्वङ्मधुवर्णो (*hiraṇyatvaṅmadhuvarṇo*) (Ā. 3-8). Your chariot, bearing food, the nectar, comes toward us. What kind of chariot? हिरण्यत्वक् (*hiraṇyatvak*): covered with gold, enveloped in gold; of charming colour; streaming with water ⟨NOTE:76⟩; as swift as the mind; swift as the wind. O Aśvins, with which chariot you pass over all difficult roads, going beyond them.
notes: ಸುವರ್ಣಮಯವಾದ ಆಜ್ಞಾಧನವುಳ್ಳದ್ದೂ in the Pratipadārtha is unclear
ಸುಶಾನ್ printed; ಸುತಾನ್ in the Pada-pāṭha

en: - दुरितानि (*duritāni*)—even the roads that others cannot cross
- अतियाधः (*atiyādhaḥ*)—you go beyond them; such a chariot
- मनोजवाः (*manojavāḥ*)—which has the speed of the mind
- नातरंहाः (*nātaraṃhāḥ*)—which is swift like the wind
notes: ತ್ರೈ. ಸಂ ೪-೨-೦-೩ printed; abbreviation ತ್ರೈ. not in the list, probably ತೈ.; reference number 0 doubtful

en: O Aśvin deities, the chariot with which you go beyond all the roads that others cannot cross, that chariot of yours, which has a covering of gold, which streams water, which has the speed of the mind, which is swift as the wind, comes toward us bearing food.
Your car, Aswins, approaches, coated with gold, honey-tinted,
water-shedding, laden with ambrosia, as quick as thought. as rapid as the
wind, wherewith you pass over all obstacles.

This Ṛk beginning हिरण्यत्वक् (*hiraṇyatvak*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra when the oblation is offered in the animal sacrifice made to the Aśvin deities; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra हिरण्यत्वङ्मधुवर्णो धृतस्सुरभि क्रत्वेंद्र भूरध ज्मन् (*hiraṇyatvaṅmadhuvarṇo dhṛtassurabhi kratveṃdra bhūradha jman*) (Ā. Sū. 3-8).

The sacrificer who, in a sacrifice in which the oblations are divided, performs for the Nāsatyas, the two Aśvins, a most abundant चनिष्ठं (*caniṣṭhaṃ*) rite. He explains: चन (*cana*) is a name for food (Ni. 6-16); so this is a rite rich in food, and विवेष (*viveṣa*) means he performs it.

He also offers food. That sacrificer protects his own son by his rites. Sāyaṇa explains अनूर्ध्वभासः (*anūrdhvabhāsaḥ*) as those whose splendour is not lofty. Or else, ऊर्ध्वभासोऽग्नयः (*ūrdhvabhāso 'gnayaḥ*): the fires are the lofty-splendoured ones, and the word then means those who have no fires, the non-sacrificers; such persons he is able to harm always.
- विभागे (*vibhāge*)—in the sacrifice in which the oblations are divided
- अनूर्ध्वभासः (*anūrdhvabhāsaḥ*)—those fallen from the rites, who do not worship Agni of lofty splendour

The sacrificer who, in a sacrifice in which the oblations are divided, performs abundantly, for the Aśvin deities, a rite full of food, that same sacrificer protects his own son by his rites. Moreover, he becomes able always to harm those who have fallen from the rites and do not worship Agni of lofty splendour.

He who, in the appointment (of the offerings), presents to the Nasatyas the most ample (share) of (the sacrificial) food, who gives (them) the largest portion of the viands, secures, by his acts, the welfare of his, son, and ever has the advantage of those who light no sacred fires.
The bhāṣya of this Ṛk is on page 130.
- सं गमेम (*saṃ gamema*)—may we be joined together
- सौभगानि (*saubhagāni*)—things that bring auspicious good fortune

May we be joined together with the protection of the Aśvin deities, which is new, brings happiness and is an excellent guide. O Aśvin deities, free from mortality, bring us all things that bring auspicious good fortune, provide wealth. And bestow heroic sons and the like.
May we be united with the Aswins, by their special protection, which is the source of happiness, the guide to good: bestow upon us, immortals, wealth and all good things.

O Aśvins, come here, to this sacrifice. O Nāsatyas, do not be unwilling: वेनतिः कांतिकर्मा (*venatiḥ kāṃtikarmā*), that is, the verb denotes desire; so do not be without desire, do not be without longing or lacking in wish. Just as the two swans come to clear water, so come to the pressed Soma.
- मा वि वेनतं (*mā vi venataṃ*)—do not be unwilling to come to us
- सुशान् (*suśān*)—the pressed Soma, with it in view ⟨NOTE:78⟩
- उप आ पततं (*upa ā patataṃ*)—deign to come
notes: ಯದ್ಯದಾ ನಾಂ ಯುವಾಮಜೋಹವೀತ್ printed; ನಾಂ doubtful

en: O Aśvin deities, deign to come to this sacrifice. O Aśvin deities, do not be unwilling to come to us. Like two swans flying in, deign to come with the pressed Soma in view.
Aswins. come hither : Nasatyas. be not ill-disposed: alight like two
O Aśvins, come to the Soma like two deer, and like two gaura animals; just as those two run after the यवसं (*yavasaṃ*), the fodder, so you, like them and like two swans, come.
- सुतान् उप (*sutān upa*)—with the pressed Soma in view
O Aśvin deities, like two deer, like two gaura animals that run following fresh grass, and like two swans flying in, deign to come with the pressed Soma in view.
Like two deer, Aswins, like two wild cattle on (fresh) pasture ; like
two swans alight upon the effused libation.
गौरविव (*gauraviva*)—The word गौर (*gaura*) is included, together with the word गवय (*gavaya*), in the list of animals stated for the Aśvamedha sacrifice. On this subject, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

इंद्राय राजे सूकरो वरुणाय राजे कृष्णो यमाय राज ऋश्य ऋषभाय राजे गवयः शार्दूलाय राजे गौरः पुरुषराजाय मर्कटः क्षिप्रश्चेनस्य वर्तिका नीलंगोः क्रिमिः सोमस्य राजः कुलुंगः सिंधोः शिग्ंशुमारो हिमवतो हस्ती ॥ (*iṃdrāya rāje sūkaro varuṇāya rāje kṛṣṇo yamāya rāja ṛśya ṛṣabhāya rāje gavayaḥ śārdūlāya rāje gauraḥ puruṣarājāya markaṭaḥ kṣipraścenasya vartikā nīlaṃgoḥ krimiḥ somasya rājaḥ kuluṃgaḥ siṃdhoḥ śigṃśumāro himavato hastī ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-11-1). **GLOSS**
And in another place also of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda:
गवयमारण्यमनु ते दिशामि तेन चिन्वानस्तनुवो निषीद । (*gavayamāraṇyamanu te diśāmi tena cinvānastanuvo niṣīda |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 4-2-0-3) ⟨NOTE:79⟩ **GLOSS**

Thus it is said of the offering of the forest animal called गवय (*gavaya*). The animals called गौर (*gaura*) and गवय (*gavaya*) (Gayal and Bos gavaeu) are, respectively, a kind of deer and an ox living in the forest. In the list of about 81 forest animals used in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, they are stated in the anuvākas from Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-11 to 28. In Kannada there are no proper names for these. गवय (*gavaya*) means a kind of wild ox. Its name is stated in the Ṛgveda only in a few places. But the use of this word गवय (*gavaya*) is found in such places as Mai. Saṃ. 3-14-10; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 16-17; Vā. Saṃ. 24-28; Ai. Brā. 2-8; 3-34; Śa. Brā. 1-2-3-9; Sāṅkhyāyana Śrauta Sūtra 3-14. This word is recited together with the word गौर (*gaura*) in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-21-8, together with the words गौर (*gaura*) and महिष (*mahiṣa*) in Vā. Saṃ. 24-28; 13-49, and in Mai. Saṃ. 2-7-17; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 16-17.

गौर (*gaura*) also is a kind of wild ox (Bos gaurus). It is commonly stated together with the word गवय (*gavaya*) in the Ṛgveda 1-16-5, 4-21-8; 4-58-2; 5-78-2; 7-69-6; 7-98-1 and such places. The use of this word is found also in Mai. Saṃ. 3-14-10; Vā. Saṃ. 24-28; Ai. Brā. 3-34 and such places. That it is a forest animal is said in Vā. Saṃ. 13-48. The name of the female animal गौरि (*gauri*) is in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-84-10; 4-12-6; 9-12-3; 1-164-11. The name गौरमृग (*gauramṛga*) also is found in Vā. Saṃ. 24-32; Ai. Brā. 2-8.
notes: abbreviation ಸಾ. ಭಾ. printed

en: O Vājinīvasū, you two Aśvins who provide dwelling for the sake of food, accept our sacrifice, for the sake of what is desired or for the seeking of it; serve it.
- वाजिनीवसू (*vājinīvasū*)—endowed with the wealth of food
- सुतान् उप (*sutān upa*)—with the pressed Soma in view
O Aśvin deities, endowed with the wealth of food, partake of our sacrifice for your satisfaction. Like two swans flying in, come flying with the pressed Soma in view.
Aswins, affluent in food, be propitiated at your pleasure by the sacrifice: alight like two swans upon the effused libation.

Atri, our father, when he called upon you and praised you, imploring like a woman who asks and who, as she pleases her husband, acts accordingly, ⟨NOTE:80⟩ while he was thrown into the ऋबीसं (*ṛbīsaṃ*), the chaff-fire, in the fire-pit,

and was releasing himself from it (अवरोहन् (*avarohan*)), called upon you. Sāyaṇa explains the next words: with the speed of a falcon, that is, of Garutmat, with its speed; the particle चित् (*cit*) has the sense of comparison. Or else: with the new speed, the speed freshly arisen, of a falcon that is constantly flying, the first speed of the falcon, and with a chariot that is the most auspicious, the most pleasant for us, come, O Aśvins, to protect him.
notes: abbreviation ತೈ. ಎ. printed

en: - अवरोहन् (*avarohan*)—(with your help) escaping from there
- यत् (*yat*)—with which devotion full of gratitude
- नाधमाना (*nādhamānā*)—who begs for the love of her husband
- जवसा (*javasā*)—with a speed like the speed
- शंतमेन (*śaṃtamena*)—that brings happiness, with your chariot

O Aśvin deities, Atri, fallen into the fire-pit, escaped from there with your help, and with the devotion full of gratitude with which he prayed to you and called you, like a woman who begs for the love of her husband, for that reason deign to come with your chariot that brings happiness, with a speed like the newly arisen speed of the falcon.

Inasmuch as Atri, escaping by your aid from the fire of chaff, conciliations you, like a wife soliciting (the affection of a husband), therefore come with (your) propitious cars, with the new-born rapidity of the falcon.
अश्विना ऋबीसं अत्रिः अवरोहन् (*aśvinā ṛbīsaṃ atriḥ avarohan*)—O Aśvin deities, the seer Atri, who had fallen into the fire-pit, escaped from the fire with your help. On this subject:
युवं ह घर्म० मधुमंतमत्रयेऽपो न क्षोदोऽव्वणीतमेषे । (*yuvaṃ ha gharma0 madhumaṃtamatraye 'po na kṣodo 'vvaṇītameṣe |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-180-4) **GLOSS**
In Ṛks such as this, the matter of the Aśvin deities saving Atri, who had fallen into the fire and was suffering, is stated.

अत्रेतिहासमाहुः । प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरंतमत्रिं राक्षसास्तप्ते घर्मेऽपातयन् स च तस्यमानोःश्विन् तुष्टाव । त्वा च स्तुत्या हृष्टमनसावरक्षतामिति ॥ (*atretihāsamāhuḥ | pravargyeṇa pracaraṃtamatriṃ rākṣasāstapte gharme 'pātayan sa ca tasyamānoḥśvin tuṣṭāva | tvā ca stutyā hṛṣṭamanasāvarakṣatāmiti ‖*) (Sā. Bhā.) ⟨NOTE:81⟩

The rākṣasas threw the seer Atri, who was engaged in the sacrificial rite called Pravargya, into a blazing fire. Then Atri took refuge in the Aśvin deities and prayed that they protect him. They, satisfied, protected him, so it says. Further:
याभिः शुचंतिं धनसां सुषंसदं तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावंतमत्रये । (*yābhiḥ śucaṃtiṃ dhanasāṃ suṣaṃsadaṃ taptaṃ gharmamomyāvaṃtamatraye |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-7) **GLOSS**

हिमेनाग्निं फ्रंसमवारयेथां पितुमतीमूर्जमस्मा अधत्तं । यबीसे अत्रिमश्विनावनीतमुन्निन्यथुः सर्वगणं स्वस्ति ॥ (*himenāgniṃ phraṃsamavārayethāṃ pitumatīmūrjamasmā adhattaṃ | yabīse atrimaśvināvanītamunninyathuḥ sarvagaṇaṃ svasti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-8) **GLOSS**
This allusion is found also in these Ṛks:

अत्रिर्नामषिः । तमसुरा अग्निकूटे प्रचिक्षिपुः । सोऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव तमश्विना वागत्य वृष्टा निशमय्याग्निं तत उज्जह्रतुः । बलं चासुरप्रतिबंध समर्थमस्मै सहान्नेन ददतुरिति ॥ (*atrirnāmaṣiḥ | tamasurā agnikūṭe pracikṣipuḥ | so 'śvinau tuṣṭāva tamaśvinā vāgatya vṛṣṭā niśamayyāgniṃ tata ujjahratuḥ | balaṃ cāsurapratibaṃdha samarthamasmai sahānnena dadaturiti ‖*) (Sā. Bhā.)

Once upon a time the asuras threw the seer called Atri into a heap of fire. He prayed to the Aśvin deities. They came, put out the fire with rain-water and lifted him up. Afterwards they gave him strength to hold back the asuras, and food. So the story goes.
notes: ಗರ್ಭೋಲ್ಪೇನ printed; reading doubtful

en: Sāyaṇa tells the old story of Saptavadhri. His rivals, his brother's sons, put the seer into a chest with care, sealed it and kept it in their own house, so arranged that he should not unite with his wife at night. Every morning they opened it and tormented that sage. Having lived thus a long time in the chest, unhappy and lean, the sage thought of a means of escape; having decided in his heart, with a glad mind he praised the Nāsatyas. The two Aśvins came, opened the chest, lifted the seer out and quickly became invisible. The seer, after being with his wife, afraid, came back in the morning and entered the chest again, staying as before. While he was staying in the chest he saw this pair of Ṛks. Then the explanation of the verse: O Vanaspati, that is, the chest, which is a modification of a tree, open wide, be opened; as the womb of a woman about to give birth is opened, so be opened. For that, O Aśvins, hear my call; and having heard, release me, the seer Saptavadhri.
- सूष्यंत्याः (*sūṣyaṃtyāḥ*)—of a woman at the time of delivery
- योनिः इव (*yoniḥ iva*)—like the organ of birth
- वि जिहीष्ट्व (*vi jihīṣṭva*)—open your mouth wide
- सप्तवध्रिं च (*saptavadhriṃ ca*)—and the seer Saptavadhri
O Vanaspati (O chest), open your mouth wide, like the organ of birth of a woman at the time of delivery. O Aśvin deities, hear my call. Release Saptavadhri also.
Open, Vanaspati. like the womb of a parturient female: hear,
Aswins, my invocation : set Saptavadhri free.
On this Ṛk and the next there is a story concerning the seer Saptavadhri, who saw this sūkta:
अत्र ब्रुवंतीतिहासं सप्तवध्रेः पुराविदः । भ्रातृव्याः पेटिकायां तमृषिं प्रक्षिप्य यत्नतः ॥ (*atra bruvaṃtītihāsaṃ saptavadhreḥ purāvidaḥ | bhrātṛvyāḥ peṭikāyāṃ tamṛṣiṃ prakṣipya yatnataḥ ‖*)

मुद्रां कृत्वा गृहे स्विये रक्षयित्वा न्यवेशयन् । न संगच्छेत भार्यां स्वां यथा रात्रौ तथा कृतं ॥ प्रातःप्रातः समुद्भाट्य निर्मथिष्यंति तं मुनिं । एवं स्थित्वा चिरं कालं पेटायां दुःखितः कृशः ॥ उपायं चिंतयामास निर्गमस्य चिरं मुनिः । हृदि निश्चित्य नासत्यावस्तौषीद्वृष्टमानसः ॥ तमश्विन् समागत्य समुद्भाट्य च पेटकां । उद्धृत्य तम्मषिं शीघ्रं तावदृष्टौ बभूवतुः ॥ स ऋषिर्भार्यया सार्धं रमित्वाथ पुनर्भयात् । प्रातरेत्य पुनः पेटां प्रविश्य प्रागिव स्थितः ॥ पेटानिवाससमये दृष्टवानृग्वयं तदा ॥ (*mudrāṃ kṛtvā gṛhe sviye rakṣayitvā nyaveśayan | na saṃgaccheta bhāryāṃ svāṃ yathā rātrau tathā kṛtaṃ ‖ prātaḥprātaḥ samudbhāṭya nirmathiṣyaṃti taṃ muniṃ | evaṃ sthitvā ciraṃ kālaṃ peṭāyāṃ duḥkhitaḥ kṛśaḥ ‖ upāyaṃ ciṃtayāmāsa nirgamasya ciraṃ muniḥ | hṛdi niścitya nāsatyāvastauṣīdvṛṣṭamānasaḥ ‖ tamaśvin samāgatya samudbhāṭya ca peṭakāṃ | uddhṛtya tammaṣiṃ śīghraṃ tāvadṛṣṭau babhūvatuḥ ‖ sa ṛṣirbhāryayā sārdhaṃ ramitvātha punarbhayāt | prātaretya punaḥ peṭāṃ praviśya prāgiva sthitaḥ ‖ peṭānivāsasamaye dṛṣṭavānṛgvayaṃ tadā ‖*)

Those who know the ancient history tell a story about the seer Saptavadhri. The sons of the brothers of this Saptavadhri, thinking that sons should not be born to the seer, so that he should not unite with his wife at night, used to put him every night, in his own house, into a wooden chest, close the door and lock it. Then, rising in the morning, they would open the door of the chest and beat the seer well. When night came, they would again put him in the chest and lock it. It seems that they did so probably out of the desire that if he had no children his property would come to them. When this had gone on for a long time, Saptavadhri, grown lean with sorrow, thought how he might escape from it, and praised the Aśvin deities. They, satisfied, came there, opened the door of the chest, released the seer and at once became invisible. The seer, delighted by this, enjoyed himself freely with his wife all night, and when morning came he entered the chest again as before, that is, like one who knew nothing. So it went on for a long time. While he was in the chest, this Ṛk and the next Ṛk were seen by this seer Saptavadhri. Thus the bhāṣyakāra has narrated this story.

For the seer Saptavadhri, who is afraid of coming out and who begs for release, O Aśvins, you two, by your powers, come together for my release to the chest, which is a modification of a tree, and separate it, that is, make it open.
- ऋषये (*ṛṣaye*)—for the help of me, the seer
- वृक्षं (*vṛkṣaṃ*)—to the chest, a modification of a tree
- वि चाचथः (*vi cācathaḥ*)—open its mouth (its door)

O Aśvin deities, for the help of the seer (me), who is afraid, who begs for release and who is named Saptavadhri, come with your extraordinary power to the chest, which is a modification of a tree. Open its mouth (its door).
Aswins, by your devices sunder the wicker-work for (the liberation
of the) terrified, imploring Rishi, Saptavadhri.

This Ṛk and the next two form the Garbhasrāviṇī Upaniṣad. With these three Ṛks the seer Saptavadhri praised the two Aśvins for the quick delivery of his pregnant wife. Sāyaṇa explains: as the wind moves a lake, a pond and the like on every side, shaking it thoroughly, so may your embryo move, tremble, go about here and there; and the one who has stayed in the womb ten months, let him come out, let him go forth.
- दशमास्यः (*daśamāsyaḥ*)—the child that has been in the womb for ten months
In the manner in which a lake shaken by the wind moves all around with waves, in the same manner let your embryo move. Let the child that has been in the womb for ten months come out.
As the wind, ruffles the lake on every side, so may your womb be stimulated, and the conception of the months come forth.
This Ṛk and the next two Ṛks are the Garbhasrāviṇī Upaniṣad, the bhāṣyakāra has said:
एतदाद्यक्रयेणासौ सप्तवध्रिः स्वयोषितः । गर्भिण्याः प्रसवायाशु स्तुतवानश्विनावृषिः ॥ (*etadādyakrayeṇāsau saptavadhriḥ svayoṣitaḥ | garbhiṇyāḥ prasavāyāśu stutavānaśvināvṛṣiḥ ‖*)
It says that the seer Saptavadhri, wishing an easy delivery for his wife, praised the Aśvin deities with these three Ṛks.

Here and in the following Ṛks the child in the womb is described as staying in the womb for ten months. Now, ordinarily, it is the custom that the child stays in the mother's womb only up to nine months. But it is seen that in that time it was common for a child to stay in the womb for ten months. Even now there are many instances of delivery not taking place until ten months. And in the Ṛgveda and in the Ekāgni Kāṇḍa of the Yajurveda:
तं ते गर्भं हवामहे दशमे मासि सूतवे । (*taṃ te garbhaṃ havāmahe daśame māsi sūtave |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-184-3) **GLOSS**

यथेयं पृथिवी मही तिष्ठंती गर्भमादधे । एवं त्वं गर्भमाधत्स्व दशमे मासि सूतवे । पुमाग्ंसं गर्भमाधेहि दशमे मासि सूतवे । तं माता दशमासो बिभर्तु स जायतां वीरतमः स्वानां । आ वीरो जायतां पुत्रस्ते दशमास्यः ॥ (*yatheyaṃ pṛthivī mahī tiṣṭhaṃtī garbhamādadhe | evaṃ tvaṃ garbhamādhatsva daśame māsi sūtave | pumāgṃsaṃ garbhamādhehi daśame māsi sūtave | taṃ mātā daśamāso bibhartu sa jāyatāṃ vīratamaḥ svānāṃ | ā vīro jāyatāṃ putraste daśamāsyaḥ ‖*) (Tai. E. Anu. 13) ⟨NOTE:82⟩ **GLOSS**

It is said that the child stays in the womb for ten months, and that the son who is born after being so becomes a hero. It is a matter known from experience that the child who is born after staying ten months in the womb will in future be endowed with strength and health and be long-lived.
notes: ಅ. ೪-೧೪ printed in the bhāṣya; the Kannada Anuvāda has ಆ. ೪-೧೪

en: As the wind, itself shaking, makes the wood shake, and as the ocean moves or is moved by the wind, so you, having stayed only ten months, well enveloped by the membrane of the womb ⟨NOTE:83⟩, come out of the mother's belly; then, born with the afterbirth, may you fall forth.
notes: ಪುತ್ರುಷೋ printed in the bhāṣya, after ಸೂರ್ಯಸ್ಯ; ಪುತ್ರಿ ಉಷಃ?

en: - दशमास्य (*daśamāsya*)—O child that has been in the womb for ten months
- जरायुणा सह (*jarāyuṇā saha*)—with the membrane of the womb

In the manner in which the blowing wind makes the trees and the ocean tremble, in the same manner, by the movement of the womb, O child that has been in the womb for ten months, come out with the membrane of the womb.
As the wind, as the wood, as the ocean are agitated, so do you,
gestation of ten months, invested with the uterine membranes, descend.
Having lain ten months in the mother's womb, may he come out happily, alive, and may the mother also live.
- मातरि अधि (*mātari adhi*)—in the mother's womb
- जीवंत्याः (*jīvaṃtyāḥ*)—from the womb of the mother who is living
Let the child who lay ten months in the mother's womb come out, unharmed, himself living, from the womb of the mother who is living.
May the boy who has reposed for ten months in the bosom of his mother come forth, alive, unharmed, living, from a living (parent).

Today, on this sacrificial day, O Uṣas, goddess of light, you awaken us for great wealth, that is, you make us aware and illumine us; for when there is light, it is possible to acquire wealth through the sacrifice. यथा चित् (*yathā cit*): just as you awakened us before, on the days gone by, so also now today. O well-born one, you who have arisen in beauty, O अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*), you whose praise-speech, pleasing and true, is for the sake of horses: O goddess of such a kind, show favour to me, Satyaśravas, the son of Vayya.
- अबोधयः (*abodhayaḥ*)—you awakened (before; in the same manner)
- अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are praised excellently for the sake of horses, O Uṣas
- सत्यश्रवसि (*satyaśravasi*)—in me, who bear the name Satyaśravas, place your favour

O radiant goddess Uṣas, in the same way as you awakened us all the time before, awaken us this sacrificial day also for the gain of abundant wealth. O you of excellent birth, you who are praised excellently for the sake of horses, O goddess Uṣas, place your favour in me, the son of Vayya, named Satyaśravas.

Radiant Ushas, wake us up to-day for (the acquisition of) ample riches, in like manner as you have awakened us (of old): bright-born, and praised sincerely for (the gift of) horses, shew favour to Satyashravas, the son of Vayya.

In this Ṛk and in the next two Ṛks, the seer of this sūkta, Satyaśravas, has said of himself that he is the son of one called Vayya. In some places it is said that Vayya was a royal sage and that the Aśvin deities protected him.
याभिः कर्कंधुं वय्यं च जिन्नथस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥ (*yābhiḥ karkaṃdhuṃ vayyaṃ ca jinnathastābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gataṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-6) **GLOSS**
In the commentary on this Ṛk the commentator has spoken thus:

कर्कंधुः वय्यश्च राजर्षि अतिक्षात् तपस्तप्यमानौ यदृच्छया पर्यटंतावश्विन् ददृशतुः । दृष्ट्वा च तावमृतेनाप्याययांचक्रतुरिति । तदेतदिहोच्यते ॥ (*karkaṃdhuḥ vayyaśca rājarṣi atikṣāt tapastapyamānau yadṛcchayā paryaṭaṃtāvaśvin dadṛśatuḥ | dṛṣṭvā ca tāvamṛtenāpyāyayāṃcakraturiti | tadetadihocyate ‖*)

The royal sages Karkandhu and Vayya, while practising extremely painful austerity and wandering in the forest, were seen by the Aśvin deities by chance. Afterwards the Aśvins satisfied them with the gift of nectar: so it is said. The matter of Karkandhu is not spoken of anywhere else in the Ṛgveda except in this Ṛk. But the fact that Vayya received help not only from the Aśvin deities but also from Indra and the other deities is indicated elsewhere:
त्वमाविथ नर्यं तुर्वशं यदुं त्वं तुर्वितिं वय्यं शतक्रतो । (*tvamāvitha naryaṃ turvaśaṃ yaduṃ tvaṃ turvitiṃ vayyaṃ śatakrato |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-6) **GLOSS**
अरमयः सरपसस्तराय कं तुर्वीतये च वय्याय च स्तुति । (*aramayaḥ sarapasastarāya kaṃ turvītaye ca vayyāya ca stuti |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-13-12) **GLOSS**
त्वं महीमवनिं विश्वधेनां तुर्वीतये वय्याय क्षरंतीं । (*tvaṃ mahīmavaniṃ viśvadhenāṃ turvītaye vayyāya kṣaraṃtīṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-19-6) **GLOSS**

In these and other Ṛks the matter of Vayya is stated. For the word वय्यं (*vayyaṃ*) in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-6, Sāyaṇa explains: वय्यकुलजं तुर्वितिनामानं (*vayyakulajaṃ turvitināmānaṃ*), that is, a king named Turviti, born in the family of Vayya. This shows that Vayya, and the other royal sages born in his family, were famous.

O daughter of heaven, Uṣas, you who earlier dispelled the darkness for Sunītha, son of Śucadratha, ⟨NOTE:85⟩ that same you, O very powerful one, dawn upon me, Satyaśravas, the son of Vayya; drive away the darkness. The root उच्छी (*ucchī*) is in the sense विवासे (*vivāse*), and विवास (*vivāsa*) means removal. The rest has been explained.
notes: ತಪೋ ವಿವಾಸಯ printed in the bhāṣya; ತಮೋ?

en: - अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are praised excellently for the sake of horses
- सत्यश्रवसि (*satyaśravasi*)—bearing the name Satyaśravas, for me

O Uṣas, daughter of the sky, you who formerly shone, destroying the darkness, for Sunītha, the son of Śucadratha, O you of excellent birth, you who are praised excellently for the sake of horses, that same you shine for me, the son of Vayya, strong, named Satyaśravas.
Daughter of heaven, who have dawned upon Sunitha, the son of Shuchadratha, bright-born, and praised sincerely for (the gift of) horses, dawn upon the powerful son of Vayya, Satyashravas.

शौचद्रथे सुनीथे (*śaucadrathe sunīthe*)—Śucadratha and his son called Sunītha may have belonged to the family of the famous king named Vayya, and may have been forefathers or relatives of Satyaśravas, the seer of this mantra. Although the word सुनीथ (*sunītha*) is recited in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-7; 1-35-10; 2-8-2; 7-46-4; 10-47-2; 3-8-8; 6-51-11; 1-62-3; 5-67-4, the commentator has explained this word as सुनयन (*sunayana*). Not much can be learned about this Sunītha. ⟨NOTE:86⟩
notes: ಸುಷ್ಪರ್ಥಿಭಿ printed; ಸುಷ್ಠು ಅರ್ಥಿಭಿಃ?

en: O daughter of heaven, Uṣas, you who are आभरद्वसुः (*ābharadvasuḥ*), one who has brought wealth: you, the famous one, shine for us today, on this day; drive away the darkness. ⟨NOTE:87⟩ O very powerful one, यो (*yo*) means या (*yā*) ("who"); the vowel उ (*u*) has no meaning. You who dawned before, that same you do so today also.
notes: ಹರಿತೋ printed before ಧಾರಯಂತಿ

en: - अश्वशूनृते (*aśvaśūnṛte*)—O you who are prayed to for the sake of horses
- व्याच्छः (*vyācchaḥ*)—you have shone, destroying the darkness

O Uṣas, bringer of wealth and daughter of the sky, you who, being of excellent birth and prayed to for the sake of horses, shone, destroying the darkness, for Satyaśravas, the son of Vayya and possessed of strength: that same glorious you, shine for us this day of the sacrifice.
Daughter of heaven, you are the bringer of opulence ; dawn upon us to-day, as bright-born, and praised for (the gift of) horses ; you have dawned upon the powerful Satyashravas, the son of Vayya.

O Vibhāvarī, you who are endowed with light. Those वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*), the carriers, that is, the priests and singers, who praise you, Uṣas, with स्तोमैः (*stomaiḥ*), hymns of praise, those singers become, O wealthy one, rich in wealth through your favour; they become well-endowed, ones to be resorted to by those who seek, ⟨NOTE:88⟩ givers of gifts, and liberal givers; राति (*rāti*) means a gift.
notes: ಅಸ್ಥಾನೇವ printed; ಅಸ್ಮಾನೇವ?

en: - मघोनि (*maghoni*)—O you who are endowed with wealth
- अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are praised excellently for the sake of horses
- सुरातयः (*surātayaḥ*)—and offerers of excellent oblations they become

O Uṣas, you who are endowed with wealth, of excellent origin, praised excellently for the sake of horses, and radiant: those priests who praise you with hymns of praise become rich with wealth, liberal givers and offerers of excellent oblations.

The offerers of oblations who eulogize you, lustrous Ushas, with sacred hymns, become prosperous with effluence, (through your favour); bestower of wealth, bright-born goddess, (you are) sincerely praised for (the gift of) horses.

O Uṣas, यच्चिद्दि (*yacciddi*): the word हि (*hi*) is a filler. Whatever these groups of your own, standing before you, assembled together, छदयंति (*chadayaṃti*), invite, for the sake of मघत्तये (*maghattaye*), that is, for giving wealth, for the bestowal of wealth, or for the possession of wealth, all of them परि दधुः (*pari dadhuḥ*), hold us round about, ⟨NOTE:89⟩ वष्टयः (*vaṣṭayaḥ*), desiring us. ⟨NOTE:90⟩ What are they doing? Giving अह्रयं (*ahrayaṃ*), that which is not diminished, which is undiminished or does not bring shame, राधः (*rādhaḥ*), wealth in the form of an oblation; that is, they sacrifice; or they give undiminished wealth to those who ask. Those who, giving an oblation, praise you, all of them hold the fruit for our sake alone; that is, they praise. Or else यद्दी (*yaddī*) is to be explained as "even though"; in that alternative the words "even so" are to be supplied in the latter sentence. The rest is the same.
notes: ತೇಷ್ಟಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ printed at the end of the bhāṣya
ಯ ಆಧ್ಯಾ printed before ನೋಽಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಂ; ಅಶ್ವಾಶ್ಚೈರ್ಯುಕ್ತಾನಿ printed

en: - अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O goddess Uṣas, you who are praised excellently for the sake of horses
- वष्टयः (*vaṣṭayaḥ*)—with the desire to make us alone worthy of that wealth
- परि दधुः (*pari dadhuḥ*)—they attend on us on all sides

O goddess Uṣas, you of excellent origin and praised excellently for the sake of horses, all those companies of sacrificers, your devotees who have gathered here, who desire to give wealth, give us abundant wealth, and with the desire to make us alone worthy of that wealth, attend on us on all sides.
These, your assembled (worshippers), who stand before you to distribute wealth, entertain towards us kindly intentions, offering unlimited
riches: bright-born goddess, (you are) sincerely praised for (the gift of horses.

O goddess Uṣas, wealthy one, bestow on these singers, or on these praisers, वीरवत् (*vīravat*) यशः (*yaśaḥ*), food, or fame, accompanied by heroes, sons and the like; आ धाः (*ā dhāḥ*) means place, give, bring. Those wealthy and rich givers who have given us, your praisers, undiminished riches, अरासत (*arāsata*), gave: for them, this is the meaning. ⟨NOTE:91⟩
notes: ತಪ್ಯಾತ್ । ಶೀಘ್ರಂ ನೋದೇಶ್ವಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ printed at the end of the bhāṣya; unclear

en: - अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are prayed to with excellent praises for the sake of horses
- वीरवत् (*vīravat*)—accompanied by heroic sons and the like

O goddess Uṣas, of excellent birth, prayed to with excellent praises for the sake of horses, and wealthy: whichever wealthy praisers of yours give us abundant riches, fill such singers with food accompanied by heroic sons and the like.

Affluent Ushas, bestow upon these (your) devout adorers food and posterity, so that, being opulent, they may, without stint, bestow riches upon us: bright-born goddess (who are) sincerely praised for (the gift of) horses.

O Uṣas, wealthy one, bring to those sacrificers द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*), shining wealth in the form of gold and the like, and बृहद्यशो (*bṛhadyaśo*), great food or great fame. Those who give us riches, wealth joined with horses, and गव्या (*gavyā*), joined with cows, herds of cows and herds of horses, भजंत (*bhajaṃta*), they would give; सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) means the givers. ⟨NOTE:92⟩
notes: ನಾ printed; ವಾ?

en: - अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are prayed to with excellent praises for the sake of horses

O goddess Uṣas, of excellent birth, prayed to with excellent praises for the sake of horses, and wealthy: to those praisers who are liberal givers and who give us riches possessed of horses and possessed of cows, bring shining gold and the like and abundant food.
Affluent Ushas, bring wealth and abundant food to those who, liberal givers, bestow upon us riches with horses and cattle : bright-born goddess (you are) sincerely praised for (the gift of ) horses.

And bring to us, O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, गोमतीः इषः (*gomatīḥ iṣaḥ*), foods accompanied by cattle. When? Together with the rays of the sun, and together with the blazing, that is, shining, pure and bright flames of fire, the splendours of fire; that is, at the time of sunrise and at the time of kindling the fire.
- अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are praised with excellent praises for the sake of horses
- दिवः दुहितः (*divaḥ duhitaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas, daughter of the sky
- रश्मिभिः साकं (*raśmibhiḥ sākaṃ*)—together with the rays
- अर्चिभिः (*arcibhiḥ*)—also with the flames of fire

O goddess Uṣas, of excellent birth, praised with excellent praises for the sake of horses, and daughter of the sky: bring us foods accompanied by cattle, together with the shining rays of the sun and with the blazing, radiant flames of fire.

Daughter of heaven, bring to us food and cattle. together with the pure rays of the sun, and the radiant flames (of the kindled fires) : bright-born goddess, (you are) sincerely praised for (the gift of ) horses.

O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, you shine; make it dawn. Do not prolong delay, चिरं (*ciraṃ*), with regard to our rite, अपः (*apaḥ*). Just as a king or the like torments a thief or an enemy, so may the sun not scorch you with his ray, अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*), his brightness. ⟨NOTE:93⟩
notes: the Anuvāda prints ದ್ಯುತದ್ಯಾಮಾನಮುಷೋ ನಾಜೇನ; the bhāṣya has ವಾಜೇನ

en: - अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are praised with excellent praises for the sake of horses
- दिवः दुहितः (*divaḥ duhitaḥ*)—O goddess Uṣas, daughter of the sky
- व्युच्छ (*vyuccha*)—drive away the darkness and shine
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the manner in which a king torments
- नेत् तपाति (*net tapāti*)—may he certainly not burn and torment

O goddess Uṣas, of excellent birth, praised with excellent praises for the sake of horses, and daughter of the sky: drive away the darkness and shine for us. Do not cause delay to our rite. In the manner in which a king torments an enemy and a thief, may the sun certainly not burn and torment you with his brightness.

Daughter of heaven, Dawn! delay not our (sacred) rite ; let not the sun scorch you with his ray, as (a prince punishes) a thief, or (subdues) an enemy: bright-born goddess, (you are) sincerely praised for (the gift of) horses.

O Uṣas, is what you wish to give us only this much? The word इच्छब्द (*icchabda*) has the sense of "only": what has been prayed for in this sūkta alone, this is the meaning. Or else you are able to give more, even what has not been prayed for; whatever is to be given, give all of it, this is the meaning. O radiant Uṣas, you who, dawning for the singers, driving away the darkness for the sake of their worldly and Vedic activity, न प्रमीयसे (*na pramīyase*), are not harmful to them: you do not injure them; you are not angry, this is the meaning. Such as you are, you are able to give.
- अश्वसूनृते (*aśvasūnṛte*)—O you who are praised with excellent praises for the sake of horses
- न प्रमीयसे (*na pramīyase*)—are not harmful to them
- एतावदित् (*etāvadit*)—just as much as is specified in this prayer
- भूयं वा (*bhūyaṃ vā*)—or in a still greater measure
notes: ಪರಿವೃಢೋಷಾಃ printed

en: O radiant goddess Uṣas, of excellent origin, praised with excellent praises for the sake of horses: you who, destroying the darkness for your praisers, are not harmful to them, such as you are, you are able to give, whether just as much as is specified in this prayer or in a still greater measure.

You, Ushas, are able to give (us) whatever, indeed, (has been solicited), and much (that has not been asked for); for, radiant (divinity), you are dawning upon your adorers, you are never cruel (to them): bright-born goddes (you are) sincerely praised for (the gift of) horses.

द्युतद्यामानं (*dyutadyāmānaṃ*): having a shining chariot; बृहतीं (*bṛhatīṃ*): great; ऋतेन (*ṛtena*): by truth, by the sacrifice; she is ऋतावरीं (*ṛtāvarīṃ*), possessed of truth; अरुणप्सुं (*aruṇapsuṃ*): of ruddy form; विभातीं (*vibhātīṃ*): dawning; देवीं (*devīṃ*): the shining उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*), Uṣas; स्वरावहंतीं (*svarāvahaṃtīṃ*): going to the sun. Such a Uṣas, of great majesty, the wise priests, विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*), मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*), with hymns of praise, प्रति जरंते (*prati jaraṃte*), praise.
- द्युतद्यामानं (*dyutadyāmānaṃ*)—she who has a shining chariot
- बृहतीं (*bṛhatīṃ*)—she who is of great form
- अरुणप्सुं (*aruṇapsuṃ*)—she who has a golden-coloured form
- विभातीं (*vibhātīṃ*)—she who shines, dispersing the darkness
- देवीं (*devīṃ*)—she who has the nature of a deity
- स्वरावहंतीं (*svarāvahaṃtīṃ*)—she who goes before the sun

The wise priests praise with hymns of praise the goddess Uṣas, who has a shining chariot, is of great form, is worshipped through the sacrifice, has a golden-coloured form, shines dispersing the darkness, has the nature of a deity and goes before the sun.
The wise priests celebrate with hymns the divine, bright-charioted, expanded Dawn ; worshipped with holy worship, purple-tinted, radiant, leading on the sun.

दर्शता (*darśatā*): this lovely Uṣas, बोधयंती (*bodhayaṃtī*), awakening: whom? The person who is asleep, this is the meaning. Making the paths सुगान् (*sugān*), easy to travel, she goes अग्रे (*agre*), before the sun. What is this Uṣas like? बृहद्रथा (*bṛhadrathā*), having a large chariot; बृहती (*bṛhatī*), great; विश्वमिन्वा (*viśvaminvā*), pervading the whole world. Such a Uṣas bestows light, brilliance, at the beginning of the days.
- दर्शता (*darśatā*)—she who has an attractive form
- बृहद्रथा (*bṛhadrathā*)—she who has a chariot of huge form
- बृहती (*bṛhatī*)—she who is of great form
- अग्रे (*agre*)—in the first parts (in the morning)

Uṣas, who has an attractive form, goes awakening the people and making, in front of the sun, paths easy to travel. Uṣas, who has a chariot of huge form, is of great form and pervades the world, spreads brilliance in the first parts of the days (in the morning).
The lovely dawn, arousing man, goes before (the sun) preparing practicable paths, riding in a spacious chariot; vast, expanding everywhere, she diffuses light at the commencement of the days.

This Uṣas, harnessing to the chariot the oxen of ruddy colour, अस्रेधंती (*asredhaṃtī*), unwithering, or unwasting. What does she do? रयिं (*rayiṃ*), wealth, अप्रायु (*aprāyu*), that which does not go away, unshaken, she makes. Doing what? रदंती (*radaṃtī*), making the paths shine; for what purpose? सुविताय (*suvitāya*), for good going. देवी (*devī*), shining; पुरुष्टुता (*puruṣṭutā*), praised by many; विश्ववारा (*viśvavārā*), to be chosen by all, she shines forth; she makes light.
- पुरुष्टुता (*puruṣṭutā*)—she who is praised by many
- विश्ववारा (*viśvavārā*)—she who is cherished by all, Uṣas
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—so as to be fit for excellent travel

Uṣas, harnessing golden-coloured oxen to her chariot, without weariness, makes wealth firm. Uṣas, who is shining, praised by many and cherished by all, shines, making the paths shine so as to be fit for the excellent travel of the sun.
Harnessing the purple oxen to her car, unwearied she renders riches perpetual: a goddess, praised of many, and cherished by all, she shines, manifesting the paths that lead to good.

This Uṣas becomes व्येनी (*vyenī*), especially white. द्विबर्हा (*dvibarhā*): of the two, the first and the middle, Uṣas being परिवृढोषाः (*parivṛḍhoṣāḥ*), ⟨NOTE:96⟩ afterwards, तनूमाविष्कृण्णाना (*tanūmāviṣkṛṇṇānā*), making her own body manifest. Where? पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*), in the eastern quarter. Moreover, she follows well the path of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*), of the sun. Moreover, प्रजानतीव (*prajānatīva*), as if knowing, making the world aware; the word इव (*iva*) is in the sense of "now". न दिशो मिनाति (*na diśo mināti*): she does not injure the quarters; on the contrary she illumines the quarters. Or else, as if knowing clearly what is to be followed, she follows the path of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*).
- द्विबर्हाः (*dvibarhāḥ*)—although she has traversed the two places, earth and atmosphere
- व्येनी भवति (*vyenī bhavati*)—she is of a very bright colour
- साधु (*sādhu*)—the excellent path on which she has to travel
- न मिनाति (*na mināti*)—she does not injure

Although Uṣas has traversed the two places, earth and atmosphere, she is of a very bright colour, making her form manifest only in the eastern direction. As if she knew well the excellent path on which she has to travel, she goes following the path of the sun. She does not injure any quarter.
